claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.7, annual return 33%, maximum drawdown 29%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.72 to 0.28 (change -1.44).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.72 to 1.72. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.69 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.72); it breaks even at 102.2 bps with daily turnover 0.14.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.72 against 1.72 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 2.25 against 1.72 in research, a gap of -0.52.
The best year gives 26% of total P&L (year 6) and calm regimes give 72%; Sharpe is 2.18 in calm and 1.35 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 1.70 becomes 1.70 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.87 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.39, 95th percentile 0.63).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.72 to as low as 0.97 (as low as 1.33 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 37% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 10% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
